references.text: Parallel passage in Matthew: "Truly, I tell you, some of those standing here will not taste death before they see the Son of Man coming in his kingdom."
Parallel passage in Mark: "Truly, I tell you, some of those standing here will not taste death before they see that the kingdom of God has come with power."

The Transfiguration on the mountain follows immediately after this promise, and many interpreters view the Transfiguration as a partial fulfillment of Jesus' words that some would see the kingdom of God.
Jesus uses the same expression "taste death" (γεύσωνται θανάτου) in John, where he says that whoever holds fast to his word will never taste death.
The book of Hebrews also uses the expression "taste death" (γεύσηται θανάτου) regarding Jesus, who tasted death for everyone.
Peter refers to the Transfiguration on the mountain as an eyewitness example of Christ's power and return, which connects to the promise to "see the kingdom of God."
The Transfiguration on the mountain in Matthew, where Peter, James, and John saw Jesus' glory – often understood as the fulfillment of the promise to see the kingdom of God.
Jesus' words that "this generation" will not pass away before all these things happen are thematically related to the promise in Luke 9:27 that some of those present would see the kingdom of God.
